root_cause.text: In io_uring’s DEFER_TASKRUN path, task-work code used the mutable `ctx->rings` pointer to set `IORING_SQ_TASKRUN`, so a concurrent ring resize could free/swap the rings page in the small window between pointer replacement and old-ring release, creating a use-after-free/race on `sq_flags`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says “task work is added while the ring is being resized” and the `IORING_SQ_TASKRUN` OR can happen “in the small window of swapping into the new rings and the old rings being freed”; the patch fixes this by adding `ctx->rings_rcu`, switching `io_ctx_mark_taskrun()` to `rcu_dereference(ctx->rings_rcu)` under RCU, and delaying old-ring freeing with `synchronize_rcu_expedited()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an RCU-protected `io_rings` pointer to `io_ring_ctx` for safe concurrent access.
intent_record.what: A new field, `struct io_rings __rcu *rings_rcu;`, was added to the anonymous struct inside `struct io_ring_ctx`, placed before the existing `work_llist`, `retry_llist`, and `check_cq` members.
intent_record.how: This adds an RCU-protected pointer slot to the io_uring context, enabling the code to publish or access `io_rings` through RCU-safe mechanisms without changing the existing list and flag members.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear the RCU-protected rings pointer during teardown to prevent stale RCU access after io_rings_free().
intent_record.what: In io_rings_free(), immediately after setting ctx->rings to NULL, the code now also initializes ctx->rings_rcu to NULL using RCU_INIT_POINTER().
intent_record.how: This ensures the RCU-protected rings pointer is cleared when the rings are freed, preventing readers from seeing a stale pointer and aligning the RCU state with the regular pointer teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Publish the allocated rings pointer via RCU immediately after initialization so concurrent readers can access it safely.
intent_record.what: A new call to rcu_assign_pointer(ctx->rings_rcu, rings) was inserted immediately after ctx->rings is assigned from io_region_get_ptr(&ctx->ring_region) in io_allocate_scq_urings().
intent_record.how: This publishes the rings pointer through the RCU-protected field as soon as the allocation succeeds, allowing readers using RCU access to observe a valid rings pointer and preventing them from seeing it unset or stale during setup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix io_uring ring resize to publish the new rings pointer safely and force user space to re-evaluate wakeup/task-run flags after resizing.
intent_record.what: The resize path now unconditionally sets the `IORING_SQ_TASKRUN` and `IORING_SQ_NEED_WAKEUP` bits in `n.rings->sq_flags` with `atomic_or()`, and it also updates `ctx->rings_rcu` via `rcu_assign_pointer(ctx->rings_rcu, n.rings)` immediately after assigning `ctx->rings = n.rings`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures the new ring state advertises wakeup/task-run conditions that user space should re-check after a resize, even if a flag transition was missed during the move. Publishing `ctx->rings_rcu` through RCU also makes the new rings pointer visible to RCU readers safely, preventing stale pointer access during concurrent lookups.

intent_record.intent_summary: Wait for in-flight `io_ctx_mark_taskrun()` activity before freeing resized ring resources to prevent use-after-free races.
intent_record.what: The function `io_register_resize_rings()` now conditionally calls `synchronize_rcu_expedited()` after releasing `completion_lock` and `mmap_lock`, but before calling `io_register_free_rings()`, and only when `to_free == &o`. A comment was added indicating this waits for concurrent `io_ctx_mark_taskrun()`.
intent_record.how: This delays freeing the old ring resources until after an expedited RCU grace period has elapsed, allowing any concurrent `io_ctx_mark_taskrun()` readers or users to finish safely before the old object is released. It reduces the risk of use-after-free during ring resize teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an RCU-safe helper to mark SQ task-run state for userspace during concurrent ring resizing.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function `io_ctx_mark_taskrun(struct io_ring_ctx *ctx)` was added. It asserts that the caller is in an RCU read-side critical section, checks `ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG`, fetches `ctx->rings_rcu` via `rcu_dereference()`, and atomically ORs `IORING_SQ_TASKRUN` into `rings->sq_flags`.
intent_record.how: This provides a safe way to publish the task-run status to userspace while protecting access to the shared rings pointer during concurrent ring resizing. When task-run support is enabled, it updates the shared SQ flags without racing against ring replacement.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace the inline taskrun flag update with the `io_ctx_mark_taskrun()` helper in local work enqueueing.
intent_record.what: In `io_req_local_work_add()`, the conditional that directly checked `ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG` and called `atomic_or(IORING_SQ_TASKRUN, &ctx->rings->sq_flags)` was removed, and replaced with a single call to `io_ctx_mark_taskrun(ctx)` before the existing `io_eventfd_signal(ctx, false)` call.
intent_record.how: When `head` is false, the code now marks the context as task-run through the helper function instead of performing the flag check and atomic update inline. This preserves the taskrun notification behavior but routes it through a centralized abstraction, which can encapsulate any required internal logic for marking taskrun.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document that `rings_rcu` is unnecessary for the `IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG` path because ring resizing is unsupported without `DEFER_TASKRUN`.
intent_record.what: A block comment was added above the `if (ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG)` check in `io_req_normal_work_add()`, stating that `->rings_rcu` is not needed because resizing is not supported for `!DEFER_TASKRUN`.
intent_record.how: The code behavior is unchanged; the added comment documents why the `sq_flags` update can be done without `rings_rcu` protection in this case, clarifying the concurrency assumption for future readers.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make io_uring ring resizing safe by ensuring userspace re-evaluates wakeup/task-run state and by publishing the new rings pointer safely under RCU.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the vulnerable race by introducing an RCU-protected rings pointer for concurrent access, which matches the root cause involving unsafe use of ctx->rings during resize and task-work updates.

The change clears the RCU-protected rings pointer during teardown, which is a lifecycle cleanup issue. The root cause is a race in DEFER_TASKRUN where task-work used the mutable ctx->rings pointer to set IORING_SQ_TASKRUN during concurrent ring resize, leading to a use-after-free on sq_flags. This group does not address that DEFER_TASKRUN race or the mutable pointer misuse.

The change addresses safe publication of the rings pointer to concurrent readers, which is directly related to the race/use-after-free window described in the root cause involving `ctx->rings` and concurrent ring resize.

The changes directly target the reported race in io_uring ring resize by making the rings pointer publication safe under RCU and by adding an RCU-safe way to set SQ task-run state, which matches the root cause involving concurrent resize and mutable ctx->rings use.

The change explicitly waits for in-flight io_ctx_mark_taskrun() activity before freeing resized ring resources, which directly targets the same race/use-after-free window described in the root cause around DEFER_TASKRUN and ring resize.

The change directly targets the task-work path that sets the taskrun flag, replacing the inline update on the mutable rings pointer with a helper. This matches the root cause involving unsafe `ctx->rings` use during `IORING_SQ_TASKRUN` marking and the associated race/UAF window.

The change documents that ring resizing is unsupported in the TASKRUN path, which is directly tied to the race/UAF root cause involving concurrent ring resize and task-work using ctx->rings to set sq_flags.

candidates.rationale: This directly updates sq_flags through the mutable ctx->rings pointer. During DEFER_TASKRUN, a concurrent resize can swap/free the rings page after the pointer is replaced but before old-ring release, making this access race with freed memory.
Same vulnerable task-run flag update: it dereferences ctx->rings without RCU protection, which is the root cause of the use-after-free/race on sq_flags during ring resize.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement updates sq_flags via the mutable ctx->rings pointer. In the DEFER_TASKRUN path, a concurrent ring resize can replace and free/swap the rings page between pointer replacement and old-ring release, making this direct dereference race with freed memory and causing the use-after-free/race described.

commit 7642e668606009fcd3fe1fc161a79ef90403d507
Author: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

    io_uring: split out task work code into tw.c
    
    Move the task work handling code out of io_uring.c into a new tw.c file.
    This includes the local work, normal work, and fallback work handling
    infrastructure.
    
    The associated tw.h header contains io_should_terminate_tw() as a static
    inline helper, along with the necessary function declarations.
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the vulnerable construct directly: in the DEFER_TASKRUN/task-work path, when "!head" it does "if (ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG) atomic_or(IORING_SQ_TASKRUN, &ctx->rings->sq_flags);". This uses the mutable "ctx->rings" pointer to reach "sq_flags", matching the root cause description that a concurrent ring resize could swap/free the rings page between pointer replacement and old-ring release, causing a race/use-after-free on "sq_flags". There is no evidence here of the fix (such as using a stable old ring reference or holding the correct synchronization around the sq_flags access), so this function still contains the bug and is not fixed.
